data.name: Lilian
data.gender_notes: Lilian is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Lilian is derived from the ancient Greek and Hebrew word 'lily'. In Greek mythology, the lily was a symbol of purity, virtue, and chastity. In the Bible, the lily is used as a symbol of Christ's resurrection, as well as of purity and innocence. Lilian is a beautiful and meaningful name for a baby girl. The name Lilian carries the meaning “Pure, innocent, lily” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lilian usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, innocent, lily and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a girl imbued with purity and innocence, reminiscent of the beauty of the lily flower and the purity of Christ's resurrection.
data.etymology: Lilian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, innocent, lily.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lilian total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.spiritual_significance: Lilian is a name with deep spiritual meaning. In the Bible, the lily is used as a symbol of Christ's resurrection, as described in Song of Solomon 2:1: "I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys." Additionally, the lily is a symbol of purity and innocence, reflecting the innocence and purity of Christ. Thus, the name Lilian carries the spiritual message of innocence, purity, and the resurrection of Christ.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lilian means 'pure, innocent lily' in Latin. In Christian tradition, it represents the virtues of purity, innocence, and lightness of the soul. This name embodies the divine beauty of the human spirit.

historical_references.reference: Lilian the Younger was a noblewoman during the late Roman Empire. She is best known for her role in the legend of Saint Eutropius. According to the legend, she was a Christian maiden who was persecuted during the reign of Diocletian (284-305 AD) and miraculously survived several attempts on her life. After her release from prison, she converted her persecutor, the Roman commander Eutropius, who later became a bishop and was martyred. Lilian is venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church.

Lilian of Parma was a Blessed of the Catholic Church and a Benedictine abbess who lived in Italy during the Middle Ages. She was born around the year 1000 and entered the monastery of San Sisto in Parma when she was a young woman. She was later elected abbess of the monastery of San Pietro in Bobbio, where she served for many years. Lilian is remembered for her wisdom, her holiness, and her charitable works. She died around the year 1050.
